# Depots
The Rotterdam depot opens at 06:00 and closes at 22:00; its cold room holds 40 pallets at 2 to 8 °C. The Antwerp depot opens at 07:00 and has no cold room. The Hamburg depot opens at 05:30; its cold room holds 25 pallets. The Gdansk depot opened in 2025 and handles dry goods only.

# Hamburg depot

The Hamburg depot is the earliest-opening depot in the network, at 05:30. [src: docs/depots.md]

It has a cold room holding 25 pallets, smaller than the [Rotterdam depot](rotterdam-depot.md) cold room. [src: docs/depots.md]

A cold-chain alarm at Hamburg pages the night manager rather than a shift lead, as described in the [cold-chain alarm procedure](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm.md). [src: docs/alarms.md]

# Rotterdam depot

The Rotterdam depot is one of the four depots in the network and the only one with a backup cold room for alarm situations. It opens at 06:00 and closes at 22:00. [src: docs/depots.md]

Its cold room holds 40 pallets and is kept between 2 and 8 °C. [src: docs/depots.md]

When the cold room goes above 8 °C, the [cold-chain alarm procedure](../procedures/cold-chain-alarm.md) applies: the shift lead moves pallets to the backup room and calls facilities. [src: docs/alarms.md]
"}

# Cold-chain alarm procedure

A cold-chain alarm is raised when a depot cold room leaves its chilled band. The response differs by depot. [src: docs/alarms.md]

## Rotterdam

When the [Rotterdam depot](../entities/rotterdam-depot.md) cold room passes 8 °C for ten minutes, the shift lead moves the pallets to the backup room and calls facilities on extension 4410. [src: docs/alarms.md]

## Hamburg

At the [Hamburg depot](../entities/hamburg-depot.md) the alarm pages the night manager. The documents give no Hamburg temperature threshold or dwell time (unverified). [src: docs/alarms.md]

## Logging

Every alarm is logged in the incident book within the hour, at any depot. [src: docs/alarms.md]
", "path": "wiki/procedures/cold-chain-alarm.md"}
